{"concepts_used":["GC-0102","GC-0046"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part51/4/4/1~1","quote":"Suspension of the opposition proceedings is available (in certain circumstances) once the option of the (two 6 month) cooling-off provisions has been fully utilised, following the filing of a Notice of Intention to Oppose and a supporting Statement of Grounds and Particulars."},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/4/4/1~1","quote":"A direction may be made for the evidence stage of opposition proceedings to be temporarily suspended in order to give the parties the opportunity to conduct settlement negotiations without the need to apply and pay for successive extensions of the period within which to file evidence."},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/4/4/1~1","quote":"The Registrar will only suspend proceedings if the request is…"},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/3/3/1","quote":"Both parties must sign the request for a cooling-off period."},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/4/4/3","quote":"The Registrar may on request or at Her discretion suspend the timetable of an opposition pending the completion of a related matter that may impact on the outcome of the substantive opposition."},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/3/3/3","quote":"When the cooling-off period ends, either by discontinuation or expiry, the opposition resumes and the relevant stage of the proceedings restarts on the day after the cooling-off ended (regs 5.16(7), 9.19(7), 17A.34L(7), 17A.48U(7))."}],"answer":"Yes, in certain circumstances—but not automatically simply because cooling-off has ended.

Manual practice: suspension is available once the two six-month cooling-off provisions have been fully utilised. The Registrar may direct a temporary suspension of the evidence stage to enable settlement negotiations (TMM/Part51/4/4/1~1). Otherwise, when cooling-off ends, the opposition resumes and the relevant stage restarts the following day (TMM/Part51/3/3/3).

Do both sides have to agree? The supplied passages do not establish the consent requirement for a settlement-related suspension. The relevant Manual passage stops at “The Registrar will only suspend proceedings if the request is…”, so I cannot confidently answer that part. Both parties must sign a cooling-off request, but that statement concerns cooling-off, not suspension (TMM/Part51/3/3/1).

For other circumstances, the Manual expressly permits suspension on request or at the Registrar’s discretion pending completion of a related matter that may affect the opposition’s outcome (TMM/Part51/4/4/3).

These are statements of Manual practice, not legislation. The supplied Act and Regulations passages do not set out the suspension power or its consent requirements; the missing continuation and relevant suspension regulation are needed to resolve that question."}
